learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solve engineering problems.
Oral and written communication in native language.
Be able to pose and plan the resolution of engineering problems, following standard procedures used in technical and scientific environments.
Be able to express oneself with appropriate correctness and precision for the technological environment of engineering.
Be able to differentiate, interpret, and macroscopically describe the electrical and magnetic behavior of material media.
Be able to understand and explain the generation and propagation of electromagnetic waves and light.
Be able to calculate magnetic fields generated by simple current distributions and determine their effects on other currents and moving charges.
Be able to calculate electric fields and potentials generated by simple static charge distributions, discrete or continuous, and determine their effects on other charges or distributions.
Know how to solve basic linear electrical circuits, both in direct and alternating current.
Know and be able to apply Maxwell's fundamental equations to basic electricity and magnetism problems.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. The Electric Field I: Discrete Charge Distributions.
Phenomenology of electrostatic interaction. Properties of electric charge.
Coulomb's law of action between static point charges. Superposition principle.
Motion of a charged particle in an electrostatic field.
Topic 2. The Electric Field II: Continuous Charge Distributions.
Calculation of electric fields using Gauss's Theorem.
Potential due to a system of point charges.
Determination of the electric field from the potential.
Calculation of potential for continuous charge distributions.
Electrostatic potential energy of a system of point charges.
Capacitance of a capacitor with dielectric.
Force exerted by a magnetic field.
Motion of a charged particle in a magnetostatic field.
Torques on current loops and magnets.
Topic 7. Sources of the Magnetic Field.
Magnetic field created by moving point charges.
Ampere's Theorem. Application to magnetic field calculation.
Topic 10. Maxwell's Equations. Light as an Electromagnetic Wave.
Review of electromagnetic phenomena: Maxwell's equations.
Light as an electromagnetic wave. The electromagnetic spectrum.
Light propagation. Reflection and refraction. Absorption and diffusion.
Laboratory practices on electric field, direct current, instrumentation, magnetic field and magnetic materials, alternating current, waves, and optics.
teaching_methods: Theoretical instruction (lectures with interactive presentations, practical classroom demonstrations, simulations, problem-solving, and out-of-class exercises involving bibliographical research)
Practical instruction (problem-solving sessions focused on applying concepts)
Personal work (study of reference manuals, individual or group problem-solving, report writing)
